peer_critiques.critique: FATAL. The demand trigger requires a mission in_flight carrying a blocked row authored before the diff, and nothing in it constrains that mission to have a consumer outside this system. A mission reading 'make the harness able to dispatch a design round' satisfies it perfectly: real mission, real block, real missing capability, clean merge. On the base rate the Strategist themself measured — 172 session files, one touching a venture, which I re-counted today — every block that fires in the first months is a harness block, and the trigger reads green while the pathology runs at full speed with more rigour than it has ever enjoyed. That is WORSE than the failure it replaces: 'built and never wired' is at least visible as a count, whereas 'built for a mission we authored to justify building it' is invisible by construction, because the justification is now a first-class artifact with a schema and a check. The Strategist anticipates a gaming objection and answers a different one ('anyone with repo-write can author a mission… it stops drift, not a determined author') — that is about a bad actor. My objection needs no bad actor and no bad faith; it fires on a founder authoring true missions about real blocks for twenty-two more days. TO SURVIVE, either of two things must be true and either is sufficient: (1) the authorising mission is itself classified 'venture' by scripts/lib/classifier.js over the paths it affects — visionary:P11's mechanism reused, not reimplemented — and a harness-classified mission cannot authorise a merge alone; or (2) the authorising mission's done: resolves through verified_by: world (visionary:P1), so the mission is answerable by something that is not this repository. Either turns a test of internal coherence into a test of external demand. Without one, it is a demand trigger that cannot detect demand.

The position says the first unattended run should be the capability probe, and that 'its job is to mint the first task id and write the first balcony row rather than to be valuable'. As engineering it is good and I will not pretend otherwise — it exercises the two non-retrofittable things at zero blast radius where being wrong is free, and its payload (three MCP servers needing re-auth, two failing outright, both second-family pins retired six months ago) is genuinely worth knowing. As strategy it is the purest available instance of what I am attacking: the system's first autonomous act in its life is a report about its own tools, read by nobody outside the system. If the answer to 'what did the company do the first night it ran alone' is 'it audited its own hands', the thesis has not been tested, it has been deferred with a green tick attached. Survivable as written if the probe is not FIRST but rides along with something that leaves the building; it costs nothing to run it the same night a real artifact ships.

Ranking the birth certificate forced-first 'because it changes the survival rate of every item after it' measures the wrong survival. Requiring a caller in the same diff guarantees CALLABILITY, which is trivially satisfiable by adding a caller — the same construction-passes defect I raised against §8's wire-then-delete, and the one strategist:P3 was written to close. The deeper objection is not mine and the board produced it in another room: architect:P8 measured that this predicate ALREADY EXISTS FOUR TIMES with four different exemption conventions and no shared predicate — skills in build-skill-routers.mjs with no exemption mechanism at all, test files in check-suite.test.mjs exempted by a free-prose map with no length floor, gates in check-gates.mjs exempted by a 40-character unused_reason, and the suite's own EXCLUDED map. A fifth instance is the disease under treatment. If the board takes the birth certificate at all it takes architect:P8's version: one hasCaller predicate, four call sites migrated, no new implementation.

The position sorts the bill of materials by cost-to-reverse, puts packs, personas, council, board, missions, balcony and FIELDS/ in the 'cheap, days' bucket, and draws the operating rule that the reversible half should be built 'fast, loose and continuously'. The sorting is right and the rule drawn from it is the one that produced the ratio I measured. git revert measures the cost of UNDOING an artifact and says nothing about the cost of CARRYING one — and my P3 measured the carrying cost being paid, in the only place this system has ever been used. beeond spent 2026-08-26, a full working day and twenty-one commits, removing a different company's brand, pricing and ICP from twenty-two agent files, deleting 1,395 files of foreign agent kit, and repointing nine agents off a directory that never existed. Every one of those artifacts was individually reversible. That is precisely why they were cheap to create and why there were 1,395 of them. Fast and loose is how 552 harness configuration files come to stand against 6 product files.

Forced expiry with a compelled disposition IS this repo's one invention and pointing it at every store is the right instinct, which is what makes this the most expensive proposal on the board. My P6 measured the cost curve it runs on: docs/STATUS.md at 637 lines, the main sha stale four times in one day, the branch name five times, the session count five times, the suite denominator four times — in every case with the correct derivation command printed beside the wrong value. Putting retire_on on packs, skills, personas, field files, tool grants and shipped-register entries means every one of those eventually comes due and demands a recorded disposition. On a machine where the measured cause of nine dead projects is the founder's attention running out, a mechanism whose output is a growing queue of mandatory dispositions is aimed squarely at the scarce resource. The Visionary sees the shape ('mass expiry in a quiet month produces a batch waiver, so stagger dates at creation') but staggering changes when the bill arrives, not its size.

Credit for the honest self-label of evidence: INVENTED. The substance: a compounds: flywheel|feeder|inventory field required on every governed artifact, with inventory additionally naming its reader, is new surface added to solve a surface problem. Its justification is that nothing reads the corpus — which is the thing in question. If nothing reads the artifacts, nothing will read their declarations either, and the declaration then becomes one more governed field that must itself be checked, expired and dispositioned under P2.

The nearest approaches are the Visionary's step 6 and the Strategist's step 5, and both are careful about what they are — a SYNTHETIC mission graded internally, and an INSTRUMENT that would read an outcome if one existed. Nobody costed this in Round 1, and the Visionary's own mitigation changes the arrival pattern of the bill, not its total.

strongest_counter: You cannot safely automate what you cannot verify, and the field's graveyard is full of systems that automated first: GSD's 40 KB verify-phase wired to nothing, Metaswarm's disagreement classifier no longer called, CAST's dispatch endpoint querying the wrong table for two months, Auto-Co's circuit breaker existing only in its own .gitignore, Ralph's judge auto-approving when the verdict tool was never called. Every one is a system that ran unattended without a control that could refuse. Under that reading the last twenty-two days built the one precondition for leaving something running overnight, and a prerequisite is not a project — it does not have to attract users or beat a base rate, it has to be FINISHED. The Architect adds the one thing that survives my Round 1 rebuttal of this, and it is narrow and unbeatable: the mission that teaches you that you needed a task id has already run without it, so a demand test run before the id is minted produces a result nobody can attribute afterwards. That is not a general argument for instruments first — it is an argument about one field, five call sites and a few hours, and I have conceded exactly that and no more. The falsifiable form is unchanged and the board should hold every lane to it: this counter predicts that the demand test is now cheap and safe to run. If the next three weeks produce a tenth phase instead of the test, verification-first was a preference dressed as a prerequisite. There is no third reading, which is what makes it a fair test.
